findingDetails.title: The trusted-caller gate is trusted-by-default in the shipped launcher, so the daemon side never fails closed
The shadow delta log writes the raw prompt with default file and directory modes and no owner or symlink guard
The prompt-time mutation refusal lives only in the CLI front door, not in the daemon that every client shares

results.summary: The documented guarantee that untrusted callers are refused before detection holds only for callers that decline to assert authority; the shipped launcher makes a _meta-less caller trusted. No spec-document comparison of the runtime ran this pass, so the protocol stays partial.

noveltyJustification: Three new findings in an uncovered dimension: one P1 on the caller-authority gate and two P2 on a prompt-bearing log and on guard placement. Weighted new 7 over weighted total 12 (five carried P2 plus the new set); no finding refines an earlier one, since iteration 1 reviewed scoring and this pass reviewed trust boundaries.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: 154 source files and roughly 50k lines under one skill with a daemon, an IPC bridge, six host hooks and two language runtimes

targetSelection.selectionReason: the dispatch named daemon and IPC, caller auth, subprocess and prompt piping, hook state handling, temp and symlink handling, and environment forwarding

searchLedger.hypothesis: caller-declared authority is the only check, so a caller that omits _meta may be granted trusted status by the shipped launcher

searchActions.result: launcher default trusted plus daemon resolution

searchLedger.rationale: fail-closed default is inverted by the shipped launcher

searchLedger.hypothesis: prompt text is persisted outside the 0700/0600 contract the hook stores enforce

searchActions.result: mkdir and append with no mode or owner check

searchLedger.rationale: raw prompt written at default mode

searchLedger.hypothesis: a shared temp folder lets one local user plant receipts the other user reads

searchActions.result: ownedFolder refuses symlink, foreign owner and group/world-accessible modes
dir-fd anchored, O_NOFOLLOW, O_EXCL, uid and nlink checks

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: both stores enforce ownership, mode and no-follow, so the hypothesis does not reproduce

searchLedger.hypothesis: a prompt can reach a shell

searchActions.result: argv-array spawns only, no shell option

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: prompt travels on stdin to an argv array

searchLedger.hypothesis: a workspace-controlled lease can direct a signal at an unrelated process

searchActions.result: kill(pid,0) probe only, EPERM treated as held

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: no signal other than 0 is sent from lease state

searchLedger.hypothesis: hook subprocesses forward the whole environment including credentials to a child that echoes stderr

searchActions.result: parent env spread, stderr ignored in spawn stdio

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: stderr is discarded and no env value is echoed into the brief

searchLedger.hypothesis: the CLI connects to a well-known socket path without verifying the listener

searchActions.result: server side hardens dir owner and mode; client side is in the bridge module outside the target

searchLedger.deferredReason: the client transport lives in .skilled/bin/lib/launcher-ipc-bridge.cjs and the shared package, both outside the declared review target; handed to the traceability pass

searchLedger.hypothesis: the prompt-time mutation rule is enforced at one door only, so a second client bypasses it

searchActions.result: parsed and enforced only in the CLI

searchLedger.rationale: one-door enforcement at a multi-client boundary
